# Intake Brief: Follow-on-Steam incentive — unlock a bundled free game in the Steam launcher

## Problem statement

The upcoming Steam release of the Tableau Card Engine launcher (Electron) needs a growth mechanic: when a player follows the game/developer on Steam, they receive one of the bundled example games for free. The mechanic must feel seamless — the Steam store page opens automatically (player already logged in), they follow, and the launcher detects the follow and unlocks the bonus game.

## Users

- **Steam players** — get a free game as an incentive to follow the TCE Steam presence; discover the engine's games.
- **TCE developers/publisher** — grow Steam following/wishlists and reward engaged players without manual key distribution.

**User stories:**
- As a Steam player, I want to click "Follow us on Steam" in the launcher and have the store page open automatically (already logged in), so following takes one click.
- As a Steam player, I want the bonus game to unlock in my launcher once I've followed, so I can play it immediately.
- As a publisher, I want the free-game unlock to be delivered through the existing bundled-content/DLC architecture, so no manual key handling is needed.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The launcher shows a "Follow us on Steam" call-to-action (e.g. a small panel/button) that opens the game's Steam store page in the Steam client/overlay via Steamworks (player is already logged in — no browser login prompt).
2. After the player follows, the launcher detects the follow via Steamworks and unlocks the designated bonus game (one of the existing example games) in the launcher's game list; verified by an end-to-end check with a real Steam account (manual QA) and, where feasible, a mocked Steamworks session in automated tests.
3. The unlock persists across launches (player who followed once keeps the game; no re-verification prompt on every boot).
4. The bonus game is delivered as part of the bundled-content architecture (locked by default) so no separate download is needed; the unlock mechanism is game-agnostic (works for whichever game is designated as the bonus).
5. If the Steam client/Steamworks is unavailable (e.g. dev environment, non-Steam launch), the launcher must not crash: the CTA degrades gracefully (hidden or "follow via browser" fallback) and the web app remains fully functional.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (`npm test`) and `npm run build` must succeed (quality gate).

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded from this list — it is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- **Electron** launcher per CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW; this feature integrates Steamworks SDK into that launcher (explicitly deferred scope of the launcher item — this item introduces it).
- **Bonus game is bundled** (answer to intake Q: "a game currently in the example games", delivered via the bundled/subset content in the launcher, unlocked in place) — not a separate download.
- **Steam store page via Steamworks** (intake Q3): the CTA opens the store page in the Steam client; follow detection must use the Steamworks SDK and/or Steam Web API.
- **Licensing:** all code MIT-compatible; no proprietary or copyleft dependencies.
- **Quality gates:** `npm test` and `npm run build` must pass before pushing (project policy).
- **Doc-update policy:** infra/tooling changes require `docs/DEVELOPER.md` and `AGENTS.md` updates (or a tracked child work item).
- **Game-agnostic:** the unlock logic must not hard-code the specific bonus game title (the designated game is a business decision, see Appendix).

## Existing state

- Launcher item CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW (intake_complete) delivers the Electron binary that boots the Vite web app; scope explicitly defers Steamworks SDK integration ("No Steamworks SDK integration in v1. The launcher must not require Steam to run locally during development.").
- Launcher content-loading is designed so Steam DLC directories can be read (option a) with structure permitting later Steamworks-managed paths (option b) without a rewrite — the follow-unlock must slot into this abstraction.
- The web app (Game Selector) currently lists all example games; the launcher will bundle a subset.
- No Steamworks SDK, Steam app ID, or Steam-related code exists in the repo today.

## Desired change

1. Add Steamworks SDK integration to the Electron launcher (init/restart-app-if-needed, Steam app ID bootstrap), keeping the launcher runnable without Steam during development.
2. Add a "Follow us on Steam" CTA (in launcher UI, e.g. Game Selector screen or settings) that opens the game's Steam store page in the Steam client — candidate mechanisms: `SteamFriends()->ActivateGameOverlayToStore(appId, ...)` in the Steamworks SDK, or `steam://openurl`/`steam://store/<appid>` external URL from Electron.
3. Detect the follow and unlock the bonus game. **Research required:** Steam's client SDK has no direct "user follows this game's store page" call; candidates to verify during implementation:
   - `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing(<developer account steamID>)` — client-side check that the user follows the *developer/publisher account* (works without a backend).
   - Steam Web API (`IPlayerService` family, e.g. followed-games queries) — verifies game-page follows but needs a server component and publisher API key.
   - Whichever mechanism is chosen must be verified against the actual Steam account model (game-page follow vs developer-account follow) before committing.
4. Unlock persistence: store a local unlock flag (or Steam-follow state) so the player isn't re-prompted; re-check on demand (e.g. "Refresh" or on follow confirmation).
5. Graceful degradation when Steam/Steamworks is absent: CTA hidden or browser fallback; web app unaffected.
6. Tests + docs: mock Steamworks session for automated unlock-logic tests where feasible; manual end-to-end QA with a real Steam account documented in the test plan.

## Key Files

- `electron/main.ts` (new) — Steamworks init, Steam app ID bootstrap, store-page open handler, follow-check orchestration.
- `electron/steam-follow.ts` (new) — follow detection + unlock persistence logic (game-agnostic), behind a small interface so the web renderer doesn't depend on the Steam SDK directly.
- `electron/preload.ts` (new) — expose a minimal follow/unlock API to the renderer via context bridge.
- `src/ui/` or launcher UI module — "Follow us on Steam" CTA component (SLL-compliant placement), unlock state display.
- `package.json` — Steamworks SDK dependency (or native module) and scripts; electron-builder config for the Steam distribution.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `README.md`, `RELEASE.md` — document the Steamworks build/QA workflow.
- `AGENTS.md` — note new scripts/requirements if tooling changes.
- `tests/` — unit tests for unlock/persistence logic with a mocked follow source; manual E2E test plan for real-Steam verification.

## Related work

- **CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW – Electron launcher for a Steam-ready binary release** (open, intake_complete) — prerequisite: the launcher this feature extends. Its AC #4 (DLC/content-location architecture) must be honored; this feature introduces the deferred Steamworks scope.
- `docs/the-build/genre-research.md` — card-game genre research incl. Steam platform notes (context only).
- No other Steam/Steamworks work items exist (verified via `wl search steam`, `steamworks`, `DLC`).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** The Steam app (App ID) and developer/publisher Steam account exist outside this repo; this item integrates with them.
- **Assumption:** The designated bonus game is a business decision (TBD — see Appendix) and does not change the technical design (game-agnostic unlock).
- **Assumption:** Following is checked once (on CTA completion) and persisted locally; unfollow-after-unlock is not detected/penalised in v1 (anti-abuse is out of scope).
- **Risk (HIGH):** Steam's client SDK may not expose a reliable client-side "followed this game page" check. Mitigation: implementation begins with a short research spike (candidate APIs above); fallback is developer-account follow via `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing`, or a small web-API verification if acceptable. This may change the UX (e.g. follow developer account instead of game page) — confirm with user before committing to a fallback.
- **Risk:** Steamworks native module adds build complexity to electron-builder packaging and must not break non-Steam dev runs — mitigated by graceful-degradation AC (AC5).
- **Risk:** Electron + Steamworks native module (Steam SDK) packaging on Windows must be validated (steam_appid.txt, app id bootstrap, `SteamAPI_RestartAppIfNecessary`).
- **Scope-creep risk:** Steam overlay for achievements, wishlist prompts, key-distribution systems, and anti-abuse (unfollow detection) are out of scope; record as follow-up work items rather than expanding this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Which game is being released on Steam? The TCE is an engine — are we releasing a specific game built on it (e.g., Main Street), or is this about the engine itself?" — Answer (user): "A launcher with a subset of the example games bundled and the ability to add more later (DLC)." Source: interactive reply. Implication: the Steam "release" is the launcher product (per CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW); this item is a mechanic in that launcher.
- Q2: "What's the 'free game' offer? When a player follows, they receive a free game — is that a specific existing game from the TCE catalog, a bonus game, or something else?" — Answer (user): "it will be a game currently in the example games." Source: interactive reply. The specific game title is **not yet chosen (OPEN QUESTION for the business)**; ACs are game-agnostic.
- Q3: "How does the Steam integration work: store page with follow-to-unlock via Steamworks API, manual key-claim flow, or something else?" — Answer (user): "Steam store page via Steamworks." Source: interactive reply.
- Q4: "What platform does the launcher target?" — Answer (user): "desktop (we will be using electron, another item covers this, add requirements there if necessary, see CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW)". Source: interactive reply. Decision: Electron stack already scoped in CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW; no requirements added to that item (its scope explicitly defers Steamworks — this feature introduces it and is linked as dependent).
- Q5: "What does 'follow us on Steam' mean technically? Steam has no direct follow webhook..." (options: web flow with in-game store open + API check; code redemption; community group) — Answer (user): "I have played a game that automatically opened the steam store page, I was already logged in and I was following the page. I don't know how they did it, but that's what I want." Source: interactive reply. This is the target UX; the exact Steamworks mechanism is a research spike for implementation (see Risks). Likely components: `ActivateGameOverlayToStore` (or `steam://store/<appid>`) to open the page + a follow-state check.
- OPEN QUESTION: Which example game is the designated free follow-bonus? (business decision; doesn't block technical design — AC4 is game-agnostic.)
- OPEN QUESTION: Follow verification mechanism — game-page follow (needs Steam Web API / backend) vs developer-account follow (`ISteamFriends::IsFollowing`, client-side). Must be researched and confirmed with user before implementation commits to a fallback.

## Related work (automated find-related report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MSI4IP6A000N7YF** – Coloretto: align player collections (hands) regardless of name/score length (completed) — *weak match (generic keyword overlap; unrelated game feature)*.
- **CG-0MQH81RIS0017K94** – Coloretto Phaser scene (completed) — *weak match (generic keyword overlap; unrelated)*.
- **CG-0MROXIJZ3004VGUI** – GymTokenPileView: card-back pile shows 'not found' texture (completed) — *weak match (generic keyword overlap; unrelated)*.

### Repository file matches
- `.worklog/tmp/intake-draft-...` — the draft itself (self-match).
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (+ a worktree copy) — generic terms (game, feature, store); context only, no Steam-specific content.

> Note: The genuinely related item **CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW** (Electron launcher) is covered in the manual Related work section above.

# Intake Brief: Challenges as achievements — sync in-game challenges to Steam achievements

## Problem statement

The engine's challenge system (per-run meta-goals, e.g. Main Street's "Foodie Row") is conceptually a form of achievement. Once the Steam version exists (Electron launcher with Steamworks), challenge completions should sync to Steam achievements so players earn persistent, account-level recognition visible on their Steam profile and in the overlay.

## Users

- **Steam players** — earn Steam achievements for completing in-game challenges; see progress on their Steam profile.
- **TCE developers/publisher** — an engine-generic achievement layer so any game can map its challenges to Steam achievements without writing Steam SDK code.

**User stories:**
- As a Steam player, I want the challenges I complete in Main Street (and future games) to appear as Steam achievements, so my progress is recognised beyond the run itself.
- As a TCE developer, I want a game-agnostic achievement layer in the engine, so adding achievements to a new game is declarative (challenge → achievement mapping) with no Steam SDK code in the game.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. An **engine-generic achievement layer** exists in the core engine (extending the existing generic `ChallengeSystem` model): games define achievement definitions (id, title, description, hidden flag) and map challenge completions to achievements. This layer is pure engine code with no Steam dependency (works headless / in the web build).
2. When a challenge is completed inside the Steam launcher, the mapped Steam achievement is unlocked via Steamworks (`ISteamUserStats::SetAchievement` + `StoreStats`); verified by automated tests with a mocked Steamworks session and a documented manual E2E check with a real Steam account.
3. Steam sync is **idempotent and offline-safe**: unlocked achievements persist locally, are re-synced to Steam when available, and the launcher never crashes when Steam/Steamworks is absent (graceful degradation, consistent with the follow-on-Steam feature CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC).
4. A single **achievement manifest** (game id ↔ achievement id ↔ Steam API name, hidden flag) is the source of truth and matches the static Steam store configuration; mismatch detection is documented.
5. **Main Street is the first consumer**: all 12 challenge templates (`MainStreetChallenges.ts`) are mapped to Steam achievements through the generic layer (no Steam SDK code in the game module).
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (`npm test`) and `npm run build` must succeed (quality gate).

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded from this list — it is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- **Timing:** Steam sync is implemented only when the Steam version exists — blocked by the Electron launcher (CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW) and the Steamworks integration introduced by the follow-on-Steam incentive (CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC). The engine-generic achievement layer itself can be designed/built now; the Steam bridge lands with Steamworks.
- **Engine-generic (user decision):** no game-specific Steam code; games declare achievements via the generic layer; Main Street first.
- **Steam backend reality:** Steam achievements must be pre-defined on the Steam store backend with static API names (App ID + achievement list). The manifest must match that configuration; store setup itself lives outside this repo.
- **Licensing:** all code MIT-compatible; no proprietary or copyleft dependencies (Steamworks SDK usage follows the pattern set by CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC).
- **Quality gates:** `npm test` and `npm run build` must pass before pushing (project policy).
- **Doc-update policy:** infra/tooling changes require `docs/DEVELOPER.md` and `AGENTS.md` updates (or a tracked child work item).

## Existing state

- `src/core-engine/ChallengeSystem.ts` — generic `ChallengeDefinition<TState>` / `ActiveChallengeRecord<TState>` interfaces plus generic selection/evaluation; game-agnostic by design ("M6 extraction" notes already anticipate reuse).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetChallenges.ts` — the only consumer: 12 challenge templates across 5 categories, per-run selection (`selectChallenges`), evaluation with completion callback that pushes to `state.challengesCompleted` and the activity log. Challenges are run-local and non-persistent.
- No achievements, no Steam SDK code, no Electron code in the repo today. Steamworks integration is being introduced by CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC into the launcher from CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW.
- CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC explicitly defers this scope: "Steam overlay for achievements, wishlist prompts, key-distribution systems, and anti-abuse (unfollow detection) are out of scope; record as follow-up work items rather than expanding this item."

## Desired change

1. Add an **achievement concept to the core engine** (new module, e.g. `src/core-engine/AchievementSystem.ts`, or an extension of `ChallengeSystem`): achievement definitions, a completion-event surface, and a persistence-agnostic "unlock" registry that the web build can use without Steam.
2. Define the **achievement manifest** for the launcher (`electron/steam-achievements.ts`): game/achievement ids ↔ Steam API names + hidden flags, documented to match the Steam store backend config.
3. Add the **Steam bridge** in the Electron main process: renderer reports achievement-unlocked events via preload/IPC; main process calls Steamworks `SetAchievement`/`StoreStats`; local persistence of unlocked ids with later re-sync; graceful degradation without Steam.
4. **Wire Main Street** as the first consumer: a declarative mapping from the 12 challenge templates to Steam achievements, fired from the existing challenge-completion path.
5. Tests (mocked Steamworks session; headless unit tests for the engine layer) + documentation (README, `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `AGENTS.md` as needed).

## Key Files

- `src/core-engine/AchievementSystem.ts` (new) — generic achievement definitions + unlock registry + completion-event surface (no Steam dependency).
- `src/core-engine/index.ts` — barrel exports for the new module.
- `electron/steam-achievements.ts` (new) — achievement manifest (ids ↔ Steam API names) + Steamworks sync bridge.
- `electron/main.ts`, `electron/preload.ts` — IPC surface for achievement-unlock events from the renderer.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetChallenges.ts` (or a new `MainStreetAchievements.ts`) — mapping of the 12 challenge templates to achievements.
- `tests/` — unit tests (engine layer, manifest matching) + mocked-Steamworks sync tests.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `README.md` — Steam achievements workflow documentation.

## Related work

- **CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC – Follow-on-Steam incentive: unlock a bundled free game in the Steam launcher** (open, intake_complete) — introduces Steamworks SDK integration into the Electron launcher; explicitly defers achievements as a follow-up; its Steamworks setup (init, app ID, mock strategy) is a prerequisite and pattern for this item.
- **CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW – Electron launcher for a Steam-ready binary release** (open, plan_complete) — the "Steam version"; provides the Electron main/preload and DLC content architecture this feature plugs into.
- **CG-0MSMGKVSS000ZEDL – Achievement give-aways: unlock three games when achievements are achieved** (open, idea) — separate item that consumes this item's achievement events as unlock triggers.
- `src/core-engine/ChallengeSystem.ts` — the generic challenge model this feature generalises.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** "Steam version" means the Electron launcher per CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW / CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC.
- **Assumption:** Steam achievements must be pre-defined on the Steamworks backend (static API names); the manifest must match that config — coordination with Steam store setup (outside repo) is required before release.
- **Risk:** Challenge completion is currently in-memory/run-local; exposing it as a durable, replayable event (via the existing transcript/event infrastructure) is needed for reliable sync — mitigation: build the completion-event surface in the engine layer first.
- **Risk:** Steamworks native module packaging complexity — reuse the approach validated by CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC.
- **Scope-creep risk:** Steam cloud saves, non-binary stat tracking, trading cards, and wishlist prompts are out of scope; record as follow-up work items rather than expanding this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Should the challenge→achievement layer be engine-generic (any game's challenges can map to Steam achievements, Main Street first) or only cover Main Street for now?" — Answer (user): "engine-generic". Source: interactive reply (2026-08-09). Implication: the layer is a core-engine module; Main Street is the first consumer.
- Q2: "When should the Steam sync be built?" — Answer (user): per the intake request, "when the steam version has been created these achievements should sync with Steam achievements." Implication: implementation of the Steam bridge is gated on the launcher + Steamworks items; the engine abstraction is not.
- OPEN QUESTION: The exact Steam achievement list/API names for the store backend (business/backend decision outside the repo) — the manifest defines them in one place; the store config must match.

# Intake Brief: Achievement give-aways — unlock three games when achievements are achieved

## Problem statement

To reward engaged players, three games from the TCE catalog will be given away free when players achieve certain achievements in the Steam launcher. The unlock uses the **same game-agnostic mechanism** as the free game awarded for following on Steam (CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC): bundled content locked by default, unlocked in place, persisted across launches.

# Intake Brief: Implement Community Favour mechanic (CG-0MSTOATDQ005XDET)

## Problem statement

Main Street gives players a single action per turn (buy/move/place) plus a Hint and End Turn. When a player cannot afford any market purchase, the turn offers no meaningful decision — they simply pass. The Community Favour mechanic adds a once-per-turn resource exchange (coins ↔ reputation) available every MarketPhase, giving players a fallback action and creating a "save for a business vs invest in reputation" tension.

## Users

- **New players** (tutorial): learn that reputation is a spendable resource that can be converted to coins when short on cash.
- **Regular players**: use Community Favour to smooth early-game resource imbalance (coin-rich/reputation-poor and vice versa) and to keep turns meaningful when no purchase is affordable.
- **AI players**: gain a legal fallback action so AI turns never stall on an unaffordable market.

Example user story: "As a player who can't afford the market card I want, I can spend reputation to gain coins so I don't waste my turn."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Engine action:** A new `PlayerAction` of type `community-favour` with a `direction` (`'coins-to-rep' | 'rep-to-coins'`) is implemented in `executeAction`, validated by the EconomyLedger, and legal only during `MarketPhase`, at most **once per turn** (enforced by a `favourUsedThisTurn` flag reset at `DayStart`).
- **AC2 — Exchange rates:** Defaults follow the brainstorming notes and are tunable per-difficulty via `GameConfig`: **2 coins → 1 reputation**; **2 reputation → 3 coins**. Round-trip is lossy (2 coins → 1 rep → 1.5 coins) so no infinite arbitrage is possible. (Producer delegated balancing; rates live in config constants like `reputationCoinDivisor`.)
- **AC3 — UI:** Two separate buttons in the market-phase action bar (one per direction), rendered via SLL zones in `main-street.layout.json`. Buttons are disabled when the player lacks the required resource, when `favourUsedThisTurn` is true, or outside `MarketPhase`. Interaction follows the established animated/sounded action pattern (popTextOrIcon + `COMMON_SFX_KEYS` SFX).
- **AC4 — Tutorial:** The tutorial teaches the mechanic with a new action-gated step inserted between T12 and T13 (renumbered T13–T17 → T14–T18), requiring the player to perform the rep→coins direction to afford the Library ($7). Tutorial scenario starting coins reduced from **16 → 12** so the conversion is required (budget: 12 − 4 + 0.625 − 3 + 1.25 = 6.875 < 7 → must convert 2 rep → 3 coins). `TutorialActionType` gains a `community-favour` value wired into `isTutorialActionAllowed` / `isRequiredAction`. (Note: the original description says "T1-T10 action-gated steps" but the current tutorial is T1–T17 with the Library at T13 — the step is inserted there.)
- **AC5 — AI:** `enumerateLegalActions` includes the `community-favour` action when affordable and unused; `scoreAction` assigns a sensible heuristic score; AI turns use the same animated/sounded path as human turns.
- **AC6 — Persistence & transcripts:** `favourUsedThisTurn` is serialized in save/load with a legacy-save backfill (mirroring `actionsRemaining`); the action is recorded as a transcript event (`recordMainStreetEvent`).
- **AC7 — Tests:** Unit tests cover: legal exchange, both directions, insufficient funds rejection, once-per-turn enforcement + DayStart reset, MarketPhase gating, legacy save backfill, AI enumeration/scoring. Browser test covers both buttons rendering, disabling, and a full exchange round. All related docs (see Key Files) are updated, and the full project test suite (`npm test`) plus `npm run build` pass.

## Constraints

- Must follow the flat-monorepo conventions (path aliases `@card-system`, `@rule-engine`, `@core-engine`).
- UI must use SLL (no hardcoded pixel positions) per the SLL requirement.
- SFX must use `COMMON_SFX_KEYS` from `src/core-engine/SoundManager.ts` — no game-scoped string literals.
- Reduced-motion and settings-panel mute/volume preferences must be respected.
- Hands/piles and card actions must go through shared engine components (`HandView`, `PileView`, animator helpers); the favour action is a resource exchange (no cards), so it uses the overlay/action-button pattern instead.
- The action is a resource exchange only — it does not consume or create cards, and does not interact with the street grid.

## Existing state

- `PlayerAction` union (`MainStreetEngine.ts`) has no exchange action; `executeAction` decrements `actionsRemaining` for purchase actions.
- Resources are `coins` / `reputation` in `resourceBank`, mirrored by a shared `EconomyLedger` (`syncResourceBankToLedger`); reputation already feeds the income multiplier (`reputationCoinMultiplier`) and final score.
- Tutorial scenario starts at 16 coins / 5 rep with a documented coin budget (T3–T17); the Library purchase at T13 costs $7 and is affordable without conversion.
- Action bar renders End Turn + Hint buttons during `MarketPhase` (`MainStreetRenderer.ts`); SLL zones live in `main-street.layout.json`.
- `MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` enumerates legal actions and scores them; `MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` drives AI games.

## Desired change

Add the Community Favour exchange to the engine, UI, AI, tutorial, persistence, and transcripts, with per-difficulty configurable rates and a once-per-turn guard. Reduce the tutorial scenario's starting coins so the Library step requires a rep→coins conversion, demonstrating the mechanic's liquidity value.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — Add `CommunityFavourAction` to `PlayerAction`, new `case 'community-favour'` in `executeAction`, validation (MarketPhase, once-per-turn, ledger check), `DayStart` flag reset.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — Add `favourUsedThisTurn: boolean` to state + setup/save/load with legacy backfill.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetDifficulty.ts` — Add exchange-rate constants to `GameConfig` + all presets (e.g. `favourCoinsToRepCost`, `favourRepToCoinsRepCost`, `favourRepToCoinsCoinGain`).
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` — Render two favour buttons in the market-phase action bar with disabled states.
- `example-games/main-street/layouts/main-street.layout.json` — Add SLL zones/anchors for the favour buttons.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts` — Dispatch the new action through the animated/sounded path; wire `popTextOrIcon` + SFX.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — Add the action to `enumerateLegalActions` and `scoreAction`.
- `example-games/main-street/TutorialFlow.ts` — Insert the new action-gated step between T12/T13; renumber T13–T17 → T14–T18; extend `TutorialActionType`.
- `example-games/main-street/TutorialScenario.ts` — Reduce starting coins 16 → 12; update the coin-budget doc table.
- `example-games/main-street/i18n/tutorial-en.ts` — Tutorial copy for the new step.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetTranscript.ts` — Ensure the action is captured (existing `'action'` event covers it; add descriptor typing if needed).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — Verify AI games remain valid with the new action; regenerate affected baseline fixtures if AI behavior shifts.
- `tests/main-street/` — New unit + browser tests; update tutorial E2E expectations (step count 17 → 18, coin balances).
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` / Main Street scene `README.md` — Document the mechanic.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Baseline churn:** Adding a legal AI action changes AI decision ordering → Monte Carlo CSVs and catalog baselines may shift; baselines must be regenerated via the existing `generate-*-baseline` scripts (verified locally before push).
- **Tutorial budget tightness:** Reducing starting coins to 12 makes the tutorial budget tight by design (the festival at T14 offsets the Library spend); the budget table and T12/T13 copy must be updated consistently. If E2E balance assertions break, they should be updated to the new expected values, not weakened.
- **Renumbering risk:** Inserting a step renumbers T13–T17 → T14–T18; all references (i18n keys, E2E tests, `tutorial-en.ts`, `TutorialFlow.ts` docs) must be updated in the same change.
- **Scope guard:** No changes to card data, street grid, adjacency, or challenge systems; the exchange is purely a resource operation. Any ideas discovered during implementation (e.g. a market "sell card for coins" mechanic) should be filed as new work items, not folded in.
- **Assumption (documented):** The action does **not** consume `actionsRemaining` — it is a free once-per-turn action available during MarketPhase, so it functions as a true fallback when the player cannot afford a purchase. This preserves the description's intent ("meaningful action every turn, even when they cannot afford a market purchase") and avoids competing with the purchase economy. (If the producer prefers it to consume the action, the change is a one-line guard removal plus AC rewording.)

## Related work

- CG-0MSTOATDT009BRX2 — Tutorial coin-budget "cost-at-play" change (TutorialScenario.ts budget table; this feature modifies that budget).
- CG-0MSXIQIPJ000NDTL — Main Street two-step click-to-place flow (same action-bar/tutorial area; tutorial gating must remain compatible).
- CG-0MRER3RE300418SG — Fractional coins (income multiplier precision; exchange rates must not floor fractional values).
- CG-0MSOKG89N001LDT4 — Festival-hold timing in T11 (tutorial copy adjacent to the insertion point).
- CG-0MSLXJCHH001DLIO / CG-0MMLR20XP1IPPD03 — Difficulty preset tuning (config constant pattern used for the new rates).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Exchange rates — The description proposes '2 coins → 1 reputation' and '2 reputation → 3 coins'. Are these rates confirmed, or should they be balanced differently (e.g. asymmetric 3:1/4:1)?" — Answer (Producer, interactive reply): "balance them as you see fit". Final decision: keep 2→1 and 2→3 as defaults, exposed as per-difficulty config constants; round-trip is lossy (25% haircut on the rep→coins leg) which prevents arbitrage. Research: reviewed `MainStreetDifficulty.ts` (reputationCoinDivisor/maxReputationCoinMultiplier pattern) and `MainStreetState.ts` (EconomyLedger sync) — rates are purely data-level, no engine changes needed to retune later.
- Q2: "UI interaction model — single toggle button or two separate buttons?" — Answer (Producer): "one for each". Final: two separate buttons in the market-phase action bar, each labelled with its direction, each disabled when its input resource is insufficient.
- Q3: "Per-turn limit — 'Once per turn' means a single exchange per turn?" — Answer (Producer): "correct". Final: `favourUsedThisTurn` flag set on first exchange, reset at DayStart; both directions share the single per-turn budget (one exchange total per turn).
- Prior answers: none changed.

# Staff job-applicant specialization mechanic

## Problem statement

Main Street currently has a single staff mechanic: staff cards that go into the player's hand and passively expand hand capacity (`handSlotsAdded`). There is no in-game staff that is employed at a specific deployed business and grants that business a passive specialization buff. This item adds that new staff mechanic.

## Users

- **Main Street player** — wants more meaningful decisions when hiring staff: choosing where to place an applicant, weighing passive buffs, and taking on per-turn salary costs.
- **Game designer** — wants a reusable, deterministic staff-applicant mechanic that works with existing staff templates and can be extended with new applicant cards later.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Applicant trigger:** Each turn there is a per-turn chance that a staff member applies for work at one of the deployed businesses on the street. The chance is computed as `(reputation + income per turn)%`, capped at 15%. The applicant targets a deployed business that has a free employment slot (one staff slot per business level).
2. **Passive specialization buff:** Each staff member grants a passive, always-on buff to the business at which they are employed. Skills are assigned from a specialization pool and are randomized **once per game** at game start, remaining locked for the full game; a staff member's skill is disconnected from its nominal job (e.g. a "Baker" can carry a "Town Gossip" skill). At a minimum the "Town Gossip" skill is implemented, firing the existing once-per-turn peek mechanic (see CG-0MSXOW6GN008ZSMN).
3. **Hire / decline flow:** The applicant is presented as a new card type that **walks on from the left** of the screen. The player either lets it walk off to the right (decline) or hires it (walks into the hand / is employed). Hiring costs **no immediate coins** but adds an ongoing per-turn salary cost (deducted alongside existing staff/community-space ongoing costs during the income phase, clamped at 0 coins).
4. **Capacity & let-go economics:** A business can employ one staff member per business level (level 1 = 1 slot, etc.). The player can let a staff member go (lay off), which costs 1 turn's salary and 1 reputation.
5. **Tests & docs:** The mechanic is covered by unit tests (deterministic trigger under seeded RNG, passive-buff application, hire/decline, let-go penalties, per-level slot enforcement) and a browser/scene test for the walk-on/walk-off presentation. All related documentation is updated (code comments, README/wiki docs entries as applicable). Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Staff applicants for this mechanic are **distinct** from the existing hand-slot staff cards (`handSlotsAdded` mechanic) — they do not go into the player's hand as hand cards; they are employed at a deployed business.
- Applicant pool starts from existing staff templates; add new applicant cards via the follow-up work item CG-0MT1CIWSD003VBPK (not scope here).
- Passive buffs are applied per-business; must not conflict with existing per-slot `currentIncome` / `currentReputationPerTurn` caching in `applyIncome`.
- New card presentation must follow SLL positioning and the shared HandView/PileView / animation + SFX conventions per AGENTS.md (rule 8, `COMMON_SFX_KEYS`, reduced-motion respected).

## Existing state

- `StaffCard` interface in `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` (familly: 'staff') with `handSlotsAdded`, `reputationPerTurn`, `refreshCostDiscount`, `actionsPerTurn`. Staff templates loaded from `card-data.csv` (`_STAFF_CARD_TEMPLATES`).
- `MainStreetState.ts`: `streetGrid` of deployed businesses/community-spaces; `staffCards[]` (hand-slot staff) + `staffCardMarket[]`; business cards carry `maxLevel`/`level`.
- `MainStreetEngine.ts`: `hireStaffCard()` (hand-slot hire), `layOffStaffCard()` (hand-slot layoff), `executeDayStart()` resets per-turn state; `applyIncome()` in `MainStreetAdjacency.ts` deducts staff + community-space ongoing costs and applies per-slot income/rep.
- Related peek skill work: CG-0MSXOW6GN008ZSMN (implement staff peek skill), CG-0MSXOWLHU0099QF6 (face-down deck rendering).

## Desired change

Introduce a per-turn staff-applicant phase/step in the turn loop: roll the applicant chance, when triggered pick a deployed business with a free employment slot and spawn an applicant card that walks on from the left. On hire, employ the applicant at that business, add its passive specialization buff to the business's income/rep/synergy computations, and register its ongoing salary cost. On decline, walk the card off to the right with no effect. Add per-level employment-slot tracking, and a let-go action costing 1 turn's salary + 1 reputation.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — new applicant-trigger step, hire/decline/let-go actions, ongoing-cost integration; `resolveIncident`-style applicant chance roll.

- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` / `MainStreetCommands.ts` — hire/decline input + command wiring.

- CG-0MSXOXN81004MW8I — Add peek once-per-turn unit tests.
- CG-0MT1CIWSD003VBPK — Staff specialization: new applicant card suggestions (follow-up, out of scope here).

# Intake Brief: Fix empty user.email in global git config blocking wl sync (CG-0MSUZASM10035QSG)

**Priority: High** | **Type: Chore** | **Assignee: Map**

## Problem Statement

The global git config (`~/.gitconfig`) has an empty `user.email` value, which caused `implement.py` commits to be authored with empty emails (`Sorra the Orc <>`). These empty-email commits accumulated on the remote `refs/worklog/data` ref, and the `wl sync` pre-push hook author-identity gate began refusing to merge worklog data, blocking all git pushes. The current workaround (`WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1`) masks the problem but leaves the root cause unaddressed.

## Users

- **Agent / operator** — needs `wl sync` (via pre-push hook) to work without manual workaround env vars.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Global git config fixed:** `~/.gitconfig` no longer contains an empty `user.email` entry; `git config --global user.email` returns a valid, non-empty email.
2. **No empty-email commits:** Future commits authored by agents (via implement.py) have valid author emails.
3. **Pre-push hook unblocked:** `wl sync` succeeds in the pre-push hook without requiring `WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1`.
4. **Local override cleaned up:** The local `.git/config` `user.email` override (which was added as a band-aid) is either removed (if global fix is sufficient) or documented as intentional.
5. **Test suite passes:** `npm test` and `npm run build` remain green.

## Constraints

- Must not break existing agent workflows or commit signing.
- Global config change affects all repos on the machine — the email chosen should be the operator's standard agent email.
- The workaround `WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1` should be documented as deprecated once fixed.

## Existing State

- `~/.gitconfig` has `user.email=` (empty) and `user.name=Sorra the Orc`.

# Intake Brief: Business cards incur ongoing per-turn cost (1/4 purchase price, min 0.25), even in hand

**Headline:** Every business card in Main Street gains an `ongoingCost` field (set per-card in CSV) that is deducted from coins every turn during the income phase — whether the card is placed on the street grid or held in the player's hand.

## Problem statement

Main Street already applies ongoing costs to staff cards and community-space cards (Library) each income phase. Business cards — the core tableau cards players invest in — currently have no running cost, making them pure income generators once placed. Adding an ongoing cost for business cards creates a meaningful trade-off: placing a business card is a capital investment that also commits recurring funds.

## Users

- **Players** building a Main Street tableau: business cards now have a running cost that affects long-term strategy — higher-cost cards are riskier to hold and place.
- **Producer/balance analysts**: the ongoing cost field (CSV) feeds the balance methodology, just like `ongoingCost` on staff and community-space cards.

User stories:
- "As a player, I want to see the per-turn cost of each business card displayed on the card art and in tooltips, so I can factor ongoing expenses into my placement decisions."
- "As a player, I want business cards I hold in hand to still incur their per-turn cost, so that hoarding expensive cards is penalised."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **BusinessCard interface:** The `BusinessCard` interface in `MainStreetCards.ts` gains a `readonly ongoingCost: number` property (defaults to `0` for legacy cards).
2. **CSV parsing:** `parseBusinessRow` / `makeBusiness` reads the existing `ongoingCost` CSV column (column 28) and assigns it to the `BusinessCard` instance. Cards with missing/empty `ongoingCost` default to `0`.
3. **Per-turn deduction:** A new `applyBusinessOngoingCosts(state)` function iterates over **all business cards in `state.hand` AND all business cards on `state.streetGrid`**, sums their `ongoingCost` values, and deducts the total from `coins` during the income phase. Deduction is clamped at 0 coins (no negative coins) and logged to the activity log with the same pattern as `applyStaffOngoingCosts` / `applyCommunitySpaceOngoingCosts`.
4. **Turn integration:** `applyBusinessOngoingCosts` is called in `processEndOfTurn` during the `IncomePhase`, immediately after `applyCommunitySpaceOngoingCosts`.
5. **Visual display:** Business card SVG generation (`generateBusinessCardSvg`) and tooltip formatting (`cardTooltipText`) show the ongoing cost when > 0, using the same `-[value]/turn` format as staff/community-space cards (red/orange text).
6. **Card display:** Cards in hand and on the street grid display the ongoing cost visually (SVG-based card art shows `-0.50/turn` style label).
7. **Testing:** Unit tests validate that: (a) `ongoingCost` is parsed from CSV for business cards; (b) `applyBusinessOngoingCosts` deducts from both hand and street cards; (c) coins are clamped at 0; (d) the cost appears in card SVG and tooltip; (e) `processEndOfTurn` correctly chains the new function.

## Constraints

- The `ongoingCost` CSV column already exists (column 28) — no CSV schema change needed. The column is currently populated only for staff/community-space cards; business cards have an empty trailing value.
- Deduction happens **every turn** during the income phase — no separate "round" concept.
- Only the `business` card family is affected (not `community-space`, `staff`, `event`, or `upgrade`).
- Existing save data with business cards will serialize correctly (the field is `readonly` but set at parse time; legacy deserialised cards get default `0`).
- The min 0.25 is a balance decision for individual card data, not a code-level clamp — the engine deducts whatever value is on the card.

## Existing state

- `BusinessCard` interface (`MainStreetCards.ts` lines ~232–310): no `ongoingCost` property.
- `StaffCard` interface (`MainStreetCards.ts` lines ~394–400): has `readonly ongoingCost: number`.
- `CommunitySpaceCard` interface (`MainStreetCards.ts` lines ~954–961): has `readonly ongoingCost: number`.
- `parseBusinessRow` (`MainStreetCards.ts` line ~99): does NOT read `ongoingCost` from CSV.
- `parseStaffRow` / `parseCommunitySpaceRow`: DO read `ongoingCost`.
- `processEndOfTurn` (`MainStreetEngine.ts` line ~782): calls `applyIncome`, `applyStaffOngoingCosts`, `applyCommunitySpaceOngoingCosts`.
- `applyStaffOngoingCosts` / `applyCommunitySpaceOngoingCosts` (`MainStreetEngine.ts` lines ~1217–1270): deduct costs, clamp at 0, log.
- SVG generation (`MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` `generateBusinessCardSvg`): does NOT show ongoing cost for business cards (only for staff/community-space in other functions).
- Tooltip formatting (`MainStreetFormatting.ts` `cardTooltipText`): does NOT show `ongoingCost` for business cards.

## Desired change

1. Add `ongoingCost` to the `BusinessCard` interface.
2. Wire `ongoingCost` into `parseBusinessRow` / `makeBusiness` (read from CSV column 28).
3. Create `applyBusinessOngoingCosts(state)` following the `applyStaffOngoingCosts` pattern, iterating over both hand and street.
4. Call `applyBusinessOngoingCosts` in `processEndOfTurn` during income phase.
5. Update `generateBusinessCardSvg` to render ongoing cost label (red text, "-X/turn" below cost circle).
6. Update `cardTooltipText` for `business` family to include ongoing cost info.
7. Add unit tests.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` — Add `ongoingCost` to `BusinessCard` interface; wire into `parseBusinessRow` / `makeBusiness`.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — Add `applyBusinessOngoingCosts()`; call it in `processEndOfTurn`.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetFormatting.ts` — Update `cardTooltipText` for business family to show ongoing cost.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` — Update `generateBusinessCardSvg` to render ongoing cost label.
- `tests/main-street/business-ongoing-cost.test.ts` (new) — Unit tests for the new mechanic.
- `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` — Populate `ongoingCost` column for business cards (balance: 1/4 purchase price, min 0.25).

## Related work

- **CG-0MRXYGM9B006I3PE** "Why would a library bring in money" — Introduced `ongoingCost` for community-space cards; established the pattern for `applyCommunitySpaceOngoingCosts`.
- **CG-0MSTOATDU006UGAX** "Staff job-applicant specialization mechanic" — Staff cards already have `ongoingCost`; the pattern for `applyStaffOngoingCosts` is the canonical reference.
- **CG-0MSXUHPGT003ZMU2** "Browser test: assert count-only rendering in game-over overlay" (find-related hit — tangential, no direct impact).
- **CG-0MS7UEUL000610A2** "When buying a card it animates to the wrong position" (find-related hit — tangential, no direct impact).
- **CG-0MQGJXW67008DZ39** "Coloretto full rules expansion" (find-related hit — tangential, no direct impact).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Legacy save data:** Deserialised `BusinessCard` objects from older saves won't have `ongoingCost` (will be `undefined`). Mitigation: `applyBusinessOngoingCosts` uses `card.ongoingCost ?? 0` (nullish coalescing), consistent with existing ongoing-cost functions.
- **CSV data entry:** The seed mentions "1/4 purchase price, min 0.25" — documented as a balance decision for CSV data entry, NOT a code-level clamp. All ~50 business cards need manual CSV population by a producer; engine implementation is independent.
- **Scope creep — other families:** Only the `business` family is affected. `upgrade`, `event`, `staff`, and `community-space` cards are excluded. The per-card field structure already supports future extension.
- **Hand holding:** Players can hold up to 3 business cards in hand (CG-0MSTOATDT009BRX2). Cumulative hand + street ongoing costs could be significant; this is a balance concern, not an implementation risk.
- **Docs:** `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` (Ongoing Cost table, income-phase summary) and `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` must be updated per the doc-update policy.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Per-card field vs. computed formula: for business cards, should each card have its own `ongoingCost` in CSV, or should it be a computed value `Math.max(0.25, cost / 4)` from the purchase price?" — Answer (producer): "In CSV". Research: the CSV already has an `ongoingCost` column (column 28) used by staff and community-space card rows; business rows currently leave it empty. The seed's "1/4 purchase price, min 0.25" is a balance guideline for populating that CSV column, not engine logic. Source: interactive reply during intake.
- Q2: "'End of the round' vs. Main Street's turn model: Main Street operates on turns, not rounds. Does 'deducted at the end of the round' mean every turn during the income phase?" — Answer (producer): "every turn". Research: `processEndOfTurn` (`MainStreetEngine.ts`) runs an `IncomePhase` each turn and already calls `applyStaffOngoingCosts` and `applyCommunitySpaceOngoingCosts` there; the new business cost hooks into the same phase. Source: interactive reply during intake; `MainStreetEngine.ts:782`.
- Q3: "Scope of 'business cards': Main Street has business, community-space, staff, event, and upgrade families. Does 'all business cards' mean only the `business` family?" — Answer (producer): "only business". Research: `BusinessCard` is the core tableau-card family (`MainStreetCards.ts:232`); it currently lacks `ongoingCost`, unlike `StaffCard` and `CommunitySpaceCard`. The mechanic excludes upgrades, events, staff, and community spaces. Source: interactive reply during intake.

## Goal (user story)

When a player boots Main Street, the Day Start banner ('Day 1') and its click SFX fire immediately — before the player has had a chance to choose how to begin (run the tutorial, skip, resume a checkpoint, or start fresh). The banner should only play once the game actually starts.

## Root cause

`create()` (and the async campaign-load path in `loadCampaignAndSetup()`) call `s.startDayPhase()` at boot, each firing `MainStreetAnimator.animateDayBanner` (visual + CLICK SFX) before the tutorial-offer modal / resume overlay is shown. Up to two banners play before any player choice.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Booting the scene fires NO Day-N banner (visual or SFX) before the player has chosen how to start: boot-time `startDayPhase` calls are banner-suppressed.
2. The banner plays once the game actually starts: (a) Start Tutorial, (b) Skip for Now (free play), (c) fresh start with no eligible offer modal.
3. Checkpoint Resume shows no banner (same day continues — already suppressed via skipMarketRefill) and discards any boot deferral.
4. Day-transition banners on subsequent days (End Turn → next day start) still play, including difficulty-change restarts.
5. Reduced-motion and replay/headless behavior unchanged (animator handles both internally).
6. Full test suite green: unit 283 files / 5244 tests; browser suites (day-banner 5/5 incl. 2 new regression tests); tutorial E2E parts 1-6.

## Implementation summary (authored directly, uncommitted — pending formal implement-skill worktree/commit)

- `MainStreetTurnController.startDayPhase(skipMarketRefill, suppressDayBanner)` — new param gates the banner.
- Boot-time call sites (create tail + both loadCampaignAndSetup branches) pass `suppressDayBanner=true`.
- `MainStreetScene.deferredDayBanner` + `playDeferredDayBanner()` — presents the deferred banner when the player starts (tutorial skip) or starts fresh with no modal; cleared (not played) on tutorial start / checkpoint resume.
- `MainStreetLifecycleManager.showTutorialOfferOrDeferredBanner()` — replaces raw showIfEligible call sites (5) so the deferred banner plays whenever no offer modal appears.
- 2 new browser regression tests in `tests/main-street/day-banner.browser.test.ts` (banner silent while modal waits; banner plays once skipped).

Removed stale, completed worktree `wl-CG-0MSW6HZ6G006PK6I-test-contract` whose `.worklog` symlink looped to the root `.worklog`, causing ELOOP crashes in vitest browser runs. Reverted worktree is gone; branch metadata left intact. Belongs to completed item 'Test contract: single-row market & hand flows' (CG-0MSW6HZ6G006PK6I) — operator may want to record there.

# Income Phase: phased card-effect animations (coin grids, synergy/rep/event contributions)

**Priority: High** | **Type: Feature** | **Marked for producer review**

## Objective

When the turn ends and the IncomePhase resolves, step through all income card effects one at a time, in a phase-based order and pacing that reads clearly to the player. Starting with base income, each affected business/community-space card shows its income coins "counting out" into a coin grid rendered on the card; then synergy, reputation, event, and upcoming-card contributions either fly coins into that grid or (for negative effects) fly coins out. This replaces the current single-fly-to-HUD collection with a legible, per-contribution breakdown.

## Users & User Stories

- **Player** — "When I end my turn I want to *see* where my income came from — how much each business produced on its own, how much came from synergy and reputation, and how much events changed—so the economy feels legible and satisfying."
- **Player (reduced motion)** — "I still want to follow the phases and see the contributed amounts, but without the coin flights."

## Problem statement

End-of-turn income is currently collapsed into a single coin-per-slot that arcs to the HUD counter (CG-0MSRGTUSK003GDGE). The player cannot tell how much came from base income vs synergy vs reputation vs event modifiers, which undermines the "watch your town pay out" moment.

## Desired change

Rework the income-collection presentation into a phase-based, per-card coin-grid animation:

1. **Base income "counts out" of each card** — for each producing business/community-space, the card's base income (rounded to nearest 0.5 after this phase) appears as coins (full coin per whole 0.5; half coin for a remainder) that animate out of the card into a coin **grid rendered on the card**. Coins accumulate on the card across phases.
2. **Synergy coins fly in from the synergy line** — coins from the synergy multiplier fly from the synergy line (shared `synergyLineEndpoints` geometry) into the affected card's grid.
3. **Reputation coins fly in from the HUD** — coins from the reputation multiplier fly from the reputation score HUD into the grid.
4. **Event-card effects** — any event card (active duration effects, e.g. Flu Outbreak 0.8×) that affects income flies coins in (boost) or out (reduction) to/from the affected business cards. Duration effects are indicated via animated text lines (see below); single-turn effects just fly the coins.
5. **Upcoming cards** — upcoming cards that affect income either fly coins in, or fly coins out (from the business to the upcoming card, where they disappear).
6. **Grid-to-HUD collection** — at the end of the income step, the accumulated coins on each card's grid fly to the HUD coins counter (reusing/extending the existing fly-to-HUD + final "+total" pop behaviour).

**Coin grid packing (per user):** start as a 5×3 grid; when space runs out, overlap/shrink the coins to fit 10×3, then 15×3, etc. Exact packing "whatever works well" — 3 rows with columns growing (5/10/15...) and shrinking coin size / overlap as needed.

**Rounding (per user, Q8):** each *phase* rounds its own portion to the nearest 0.5 for the coins shown in the grid. The HUD / credited total still uses the exact fractional value (current behaviour preserved).

**Phasing (per user, Q3):** phase-based — all cards show base alongside, then all cards' synergy, then all cards' reputation, then each event, then upcoming-card effects. Each phase lasts ~2–3 seconds. **Reduced motion keeps the phases (same sequence + pacing) but removes the coin animation** (no flights / count-out tweens); the per-phase rounded values still appear.

**Duration-effect text lines (Upcoming panel):** for event cards with a duration, indicate their effect via an animated text line — on a *new* card the effect text animates in one letter at a time with a grow/shrink animation. Then, for each line (new and pre-existing), coins fly to/from the affected business cards. *(The Upcoming-deck-as-face-down-single-card redesign that frees the panel space is a SEPARATE work item — CG-0MSXIQDI4007K6N0 is unrelated (HUD decimals); the deck redesign has no ID yet and is out of scope here.)* This item assumes the panel already has room for these effect lines; if it does not yet, this item proceeds with the best available placement and the deck redesign is tracked separately.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. End-of-turn income walks through phases in order (base → synergy → reputation → events → upcoming), each ~2–3s, with on-card coin grids that accumulate rounded coins per phase (nearest 0.5 per phase).
2. Base coins "count out" of each producing card into its grid; synergy coins fly in from the synergy line; reputation coins fly in from the reputation HUD; event/upcoming effects fly coins in or out to/from the appropriate cards.
3. Grid packing scales from 5×3 to 10×3 to 15×3 by shrinking/overlapping coins as space requires; overflow is visible, not clipped.
4. At the end, grid coins fly to the HUD coins counter with the existing final "+total" pop and coin-pop SFX (extending CG-0MSRGTUSK003GDGE); the credited HUD total is unchanged (exact fractional total preserved).
5. Duration-effect events show an animated effect line (one-letter grow/shrink reveal for new cards) with coins flying to/from affected businesses; single-turn events just fly coins.
6. Reduced motion keeps the same phases and pacing but strips coin animations (text/phase progression only); replay/headless modes are unaffected (no rendering/audio — documented exemption).
7. New/extended unit + browser tests cover phase ordering, per-phase rounding, grid packing stress (15×3+), event/upcoming fly-in/out, and reduced-motion path.
8. All related documentation updated (code comments, `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md`, scene README).

## Constraints

- Presentation-only VFX: never mutates game state, transcript, or turn flow (AGENTS.md rule 8). Must remain non-blocking like the current animation (runs inside the turn-advance window; failures swallowed).
- Reuse existing helpers: `moveGameObject`, `popTextOrIcon`, `SoundManager`/`SFX_KEYS` (`COMMON_SFX_KEYS` convention), `synergyLineEndpoints`, per-slot data from `applyIncome()`/`IncomeResult.breakdown`.
- Respect reduced-motion (SettingsStore / `prefers-reduced-motion`) and headless/replay exemption.
- No new SFX keys unless unavoidable; prefer existing `sfx-coin-pop` etc.
- Must build on / not regress CG-0MSRGTUSK003GDGE (existing fly-to-HUD) and CG-0MSRGUFZ2001ELSR (synergy formation animation).

## Existing state

- `applyIncome()` in `MainStreetAdjacency.ts` returns `IncomeResult.breakdown` (`SlotIncome[]`: `slotIndex`, `businessName`, `baseIncome`, `synergyBonus`, `total`) + `handSynergyTotal`; applies per-slot `income-multiplier` active effects, then the reputation multiplier to the total (exact fractional coins).
- `MainStreetAnimator.animateIncomeCollection()` (from CG-0MSRGTUSK003GDGE) flies one coin per producing slot + rep pips to HUD, with final pop; `incomeCollectionActive` flag suppresses the immediate HUD delta pop.
- `synergyLineEndpoints()` shared by renderer + animator for synergy-line geometry (p1/p2/mid).
- `ActiveEffect` system (`income-multiplier` / `rep-multiplier`) with `applyActiveEffectMultiplier()`; duration events e.g. Flu Outbreak (0.8×/5 turns), Recession (0.7×/4), Tourist Season (1.15×/3), Labor Shortage (0.9×/3).
- The "Upcoming" panel (`MainStreetRenderer`) shows the incident queue (2 face-up cards + deck) + ⚠ active-effect duration lines.
- HUD geometry mirrors: coins label at `gameW*0.25 + 70`, rep label at strip centre (`gameW*0.5`), `hudY` from layout.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetAnimator.ts` — new `animateIncomePhases()` (or rework `animateIncomeCollection`) implementing the phased coin-grid + fly-in/out sequence; grid-packing helper.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAdjacency.ts` — expose/derive per-slot base/synergy/rep/event contribution breakdown for the phases (likely extend `applyIncome`/`IncomeResult` with richer per-phase data).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — `processEndOfTurn()` / `applyIncome()` — surface per-phase contributions (base, synergy, rep from `applyReputationMultiplier`, event deltas) for the animation.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetDifficulty.ts` — `reputationCoinMultiplier()` — source of the rep-coins fly-in amount.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` / `activeEffects` — identify income-affecting event/upcoming cards for fly-in/out.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` — Upcoming panel effect-line placement; HUD target coords; on-card grid anchoring.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts` — orchestrate the phased animation in `endTurn()` income presentation.
- `src/core-engine/ActiveEffect.ts` — reference for `income-multiplier` / `applyActiveEffectMultiplier`.
- `tests/main-street/` — phase-ordering, rounding, grid-packing, reduced-motion tests.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Grid space / readability** — on-card coin grids may visually clutter small card faces; the 5×3→10×3→15×3 overlap/shrink packing may become hard to read at high income. Mitigate: half-coin vs full-coin sizing, controlled overlap, overflow label. (Spike if needed.)
- **Phase timing vs turn pacing** — 2–3s × several phases could lengthen end-of-turn. Reduced-motion retains phases; keep total within acceptable bounds and non-blocking. Player may find 5+ phases too slow — may need a cap/condense for cards with no contributions in a phase.
- **Rounding drift** — per-phase nearest-0.5 rounding means displayed coins may not sum exactly to the exact credited fractional total; the HUD shows the exact total (documented as intended, Q8).
- **Panel space for effect lines** — the Upcoming-deck redesign (face-down single deck) that frees space is a separate work item; if space isn't ready, effect lines may need a temporary placement. Track the deck redesign as a child/related item.
- **Scope creep** — remain a presentation-only income-animation feature; do not include the deck redesign, Community Favour, HUD decimals, or other economy changes. Log extra opportunities as linked work items, not scope.

## Related work

- CG-0MSRGTUSK003GDGE "Animate end-of-turn income collection (coin fly-to-HUD)" (completed) — base the phased animation on this.
- CG-0MSRGUFZ2001ELSR "Synergy link formation animation" (completed) — synergy-line geometry reuse.
- CG-0MSX2PI7X002014B / CG-0MSX2PNSJ000YDM0 "synergyLineEndpoints" — shared synergy geometry helper.

# Main Street: Upcoming panel — replace face-down deck card with compact deck counter

## Problem statement

The Upcoming/incident panel dedicates ~70px to a face-down card-back image plus ~12px for deck-count text, leaving insufficient vertical space for the duration-effect text lines that the income-phase animation (CG-0MT23O6W8003AXWJ) needs to display per-affected business card.

## Users & User Stories

- **Player (income-phase visibility):** "When my turn's income resolves, I want to see the duration-effect text lines for upcoming cards without the panel overflowing or the active-effect lines disappearing."
- **Player (reduced motion):** "I want the panel layout to remain readable without animation — the deck counter should be clearly visible and the effect text should be legible."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The face-down card-back image in the Upcoming panel is replaced by a compact deck counter (rounded rectangle with card icon and count number) that fits within ~24px of vertical space.
2. The panel height shrinks by at least 50px (the ~70px card-back + ~12px text, minus the ~24px counter), making that space available for income-phase duration-effect text lines.
3. The deck counter updates reactively whenever `state.incidentDeck.length` changes (e.g., cards drawn, deck reshuffled).
4. The deck counter's click/tap area (if any) preserves existing tooltip behaviour — clicking the counter shows the remaining deck count, or the panel has no interactive elements (no-click, pass-through).
5. Reduced-motion mode renders the deck counter without animation; the visual design is identical to full-motion (no animation = no layout difference).
6. All unit + browser tests pass: layout geometry tests (panel height, card-center calculation compatibility with `getFrontIncidentCardCenter()`), deck counter render/update, and the income-phase dependency (CG-0MT23O6W8003AXWJ).

## Constraints

- **Panel width unchanged:** Only vertical space is affected.
- **`getFrontIncidentCardCenter()` compatibility:** The incident-reveal flight and staff-peek reveal (CG-0MSXOWLHU0099QF6 / CG-0MSXOW6GN008ZSMN) use this method to get the card center for animation origins. If the counter changes the vertical centering math, update the method to return the same logical origin (the position where the face-down deck would have been centred).
- **SLL layout binding:** The panel height is driven by the SLL layout (`MAIN_STREET_SLL_LAYOUT` zone `incidentQueue`). If the SLL zone has a fixed height, either: (a) the zone height is already a max-height / min-height constraint (preferred), or (b) the deck counter is placed within the existing zone with overflow clipped (documented limitation).
- **No new SFX keys.** The deck counter is a static/non-interactive element — no sound effects.
- **Re-use existing SVG rasterisation:** If the card icon needs to be an SVG, use `SvgHelpers` / `makeTextureKey()` pattern from `GymSvgHelpersScene`.
- **Headless/replay exemption:** No rendering changes visible in headless/replay modes.

## Existing state

- `refreshIncidentQueue()` in `MainStreetRenderer.ts` renders: title bar (22px) → face-down card-back (~69px) → deck count text (~12px) → active-effect lines (16px × N + 16px overhead) → bottom padding (8px).
- `getFrontIncidentCardCenter()` returns the logical center of the face-down card for animation purposes.
- Constants: `BASE_QUEUE_CARD_W = 120`, `BASE_QUEUE_CARD_H = 69`.
- Parent work item (CG-0MT23O6W8003AXWJ) adds income-phase duration-effect lines to the panel.

## Desired change

1. **Remove** the face-down card-back SVG render and the separate deck-count text label from `refreshIncidentQueue()`.
2. **Add** a compact deck counter: a small rounded rectangle (~100px wide × 20px tall) containing a small card-icon (12×12px) on the left and the count number (e.g., "Deck: 5") in 10px text on the right.
3. **Update** `getFrontIncidentCardCenter()` if the counter's vertical centre differs from the old card-back centre; ensure incident-reveal animations still target the correct origin.
4. **Ensure** the panel's dynamic height calculation accounts for the new counter's reduced height.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` — `refreshIncidentQueue()` (deck counter replacement), `getFrontIncidentCardCenter()` (origin math)
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetConstants.ts` — constants (if new counter dimensions need constants)
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetLayoutAdapter.ts` — SLL zone height binding (if the incidentQueue zone needs adjustment)

## Related work

- **CG-0MT23O6W8003AXWJ** "Income Phase: phased card-effect animations" (blocked-by this item) — needs the freed panel space for duration-effect text lines.
- **CG-0MSXOWLHU0099QF6** / **CG-0MSXOW6GN008ZSMN** — incident-reveal flight and staff-peek reveal; must remain compatible with `getFrontIncidentCardCenter()` after deck counter changes.

## Risks & assumptions

- **SLL zone height rigidity:** If the `incidentQueue` SLL zone has a fixed pixel height, reducing the panel's internal content won't shrink the zone itself — the extra space may be unused. Mitigation: inspect SLL zone height type; if fixed, the zone height can be left as-is (no regression), or adjusted if it's a max-height constraint.
- **`getFrontIncidentCardCenter()` origin shift:** Removing the ~69px card-back and replacing it with a ~20px counter shifts the visual centre. Mitigation: keep the counter centred at the same Y origin as the old card-back, so animation targets are unchanged.
- **Scope creep:** This is a pure visual/layout change. Do not include: changing incident-draw logic, changing active-effect display, adding new interaction patterns, or modifying the incident deck draw animation.

# Community Favour — Engine Action, State, and Config

## Goal
Implement the core `community-favour` player action type: exchange coins ↔ reputation with per-difficulty configurable rates, MarketPhase gating, and a once-per-turn guard.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — PlayerAction union:** A new `CommunityFavourAction` variant is added to the `PlayerAction` union in `MainStreetEngine.ts`:
  ```
  | { type: 'community-favour'; direction: 'coins-to-rep' | 'rep-to-coins' }
  ```

- **AC2 — executeAction case:** A `case 'community-favour'` is added to `executeAction()` that:
  - Validates the state is in `MarketPhase` (throws if not).
  - Checks `state.favourUsedThisTurn` is `false` (throws if true).
  - Validates resource sufficiency via the `EconomyLedger`:
    - `coins-to-rep`: checks `coins >= favourCoinsToRepCost`.
    - `rep-to-coins`: checks `reputation >= favourRepToCoinsRepCost`.
  - Applies the exchange:
    - `coins-to-rep`: subtracts `favourCoinsToRepCost` coins, adds `1` reputation.
    - `rep-to-coins`: subtracts `favourRepToCoinsRepCost` reputation, adds `favourRepToCoinsCoinGain` coins.
  - Sets `state.favourUsedThisTurn = true`.
  - Does **not** decrement `actionsRemaining` (free once-per-turn action).

- **AC3 — State field:** `favourUsedThisTurn: boolean` is added to `MainStreetState` and the serialized state `MainStreetSerializedState`.

- **AC4 — DayStart reset:** In `executeDayStart()`, `state.favourUsedThisTurn` is reset to `false` (alongside `actionsRemaining` reset).

- **AC5 — GameConfig constants:** Per-difficulty exchange rates are added to `GameConfig` and all presets in `MainStreetDifficulty.ts`:
  - `favourCoinsToRepCost: number` — coins consumed for 1 rep (default: 2).
  - `favourRepToCoinsRepCost: number` — reputation consumed for coin gain (default: 2).
  - `favourRepToCoinsCoinGain: number` — coins gained when spending rep (default: 3).
  - All 4 presets (easy, normal, medium, hard) include these values.

- **AC6 — MarketPhase gating:** The action is only legal during `MarketPhase`; the `case` throws an appropriate error for other phases.

- **AC7 — Once-per-turn enforcement:** The `favourUsedThisTurn` flag prevents a second exchange until the next `DayStart`.

## Key Files
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — PlayerAction union, case handler, executeAction logic
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — favourUsedThisTurn field, serialization, DayStart reset
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetDifficulty.ts` — GameConfig constants and all presets

## Goal
Add the `community-favour` action to the AI decision-making so AI turns never stall on an unaffordable market and use the legal fallback action.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — enumerateLegalActions:** `enumerateLegalActions(state)` in `MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` includes the `community-favour` action for both directions when:
  - The state is in `MarketPhase`; AND

# Problem Statement

When a business card is upgraded (e.g., Bakery → Patisserie), the card's displayed name overlay always shows the original business name ("Bakery") instead of the upgraded name ("Patisserie"). This is a visual bug that misrepresents the current state of the business on the street grid.

# Users & User Stories

- **As a player**, I want the upgraded business name to be displayed on the card so I can clearly see which version of the business I have.
- **As a player**, I expect the card to show "Patisserie" after applying the "Upgrade to Patisserie" card to my Bakery, not "Bakery" as it did before.

# Acceptance Criteria

1. When an upgrade is applied to a business card, the name overlay on the card reflects the upgraded name (e.g., "Patisserie" instead of "Bakery").
2. The upgraded name is computed dynamically from the applied upgrade cards — no hard-coded name values on BusinessCard instances.
3. Multi-level upgrades display the name from the **most recently applied** upgrade (set in `displayName` each time `purchaseUpgrade()` runs).
4. Base (un-upgraded) cards display their original `name` as before — no overlay shown.
5. The fix works for all business upgrade paths in the game (Bakery→Patisserie, Diner→Bistro, etc.)
6. `buildUpgradeOverlaySpec` unit tests cover both base cards (no name overlay) and upgraded cards (correct upgraded name displayed).
7. All existing tests pass after the change.

# Constraints

- The `BusinessCard.name` field is `readonly` in the TypeScript interface — the fix must not make it mutable. A separate display-name mechanism is required.
- `buildUpgradeOverlaySpec()` only receives a `BusinessCard`, not the upgrade templates — the display name must be pre-computed and stored on the BusinessCard during `purchaseUpgrade()`.
- The fix should be minimal: touch only the BusinessCard interface, `purchaseUpgrade()`, and `buildUpgradeOverlaySpec()`.
- The solution must be data-driven where possible (driven by CSV card data), not hard-coded logic.

# Existing State

- `BusinessCard` has a `readonly name: string` (original business name) and `level: number` (upgrade level), plus `appliedUpgrades: string[]` (IDs of applied upgrades).
- `UpgradeCard` has a `name: string` (e.g., "Upgrade to Patisserie") and `targetBusiness: string` (e.g., "Bakery").
- `purchaseUpgrade()` in `MainStreetMarket.ts` updates `business.level`, `incomeBonus`, `synergyRangeBonus`, `reputationBonus`, and `appliedUpgrades` — but **never updates any display name**.
- `buildUpgradeOverlaySpec()` in `UpgradeOverlaySpec.ts` computes the name overlay text as `biz.name` (the original, un-upgraded name).
- Card data CSV column `name` on upgrade cards uses format "Upgrade to <new name>" (e.g., "Upgrade to Patisserie").

# Desired Change

Add a `displayName` field to `BusinessCard` and populate it when upgrades are applied:

1. Add `displayName?: string` (optional) to the `BusinessCard` interface.
2. Add a `newDisplayName` field to the `UpgradeCard` interface and CSV column, storing the business's new name directly (e.g., "Patisserie").
3. In `purchaseUpgrade()`, after applying the upgrade, set `business.displayName = card.newDisplayName`.
4. In `buildUpgradeOverlaySpec()`, use `biz.displayName ?? biz.name` for the name overlay text.

This is a single-source-of-truth approach: each upgrade card declares the new business name, and the BusinessCard tracks its current display name.

# Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` — `UpgradeCard` interface (add field)
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/UpgradeOverlaySpec.ts` — `buildUpgradeOverlaySpec()` (compute name from applied upgrades)
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` — `applyUpgradeOverlays()` (uses spec from above; likely no change needed)
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMarket.ts` — `purchaseUpgrade()` (may need to store new name on BusinessCard, depending on approach)
- `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` — upgrade card definitions (add `newDisplayName` column if Option A)

# Related Work

- **CG-0MSKSJ9SS0069ZWT**: Main Street tutorial: full text review and step restructure (references patisserie upgrade in tutorial context).

---

# Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "Should the BusinessCard.name field be updated, or should a separate display name mechanism be used?"
  - A: A separate display name mechanism is needed since `BusinessCard.name` is `readonly` and used for identification/logic elsewhere. The overlay should derive the display name from applied upgrades.
  - Evidence: TypeScript interface definition in `MainStreetCards.ts` line 234 (`readonly name: string`).

- Q: "Should the new name come from the upgrade card's name field, or a dedicated field?"
  - A: A dedicated field (`newDisplayName` on UpgradeCard) is preferred for clarity and to avoid fragile string parsing of "Upgrade to X" patterns.
